t: What if every dollar you spent cost you one minute of your life?
You tap your card for a coffee. Five dollars.
Beep. And the number above your head drops by five.
Not five dollars. Five minutes. Of your life.
The average new car in America costs about forty-eight thousand dollars. That's thirty-three days of your life. For a car.
It's not your bill. It's Mom's.
Her surgery. Ninety thousand dollars the insurance won't cover. Due Friday.
Ninety thousand minutes. That's sixty-two days of your life.
At the front desk, you open the payment screen. Ninety thousand. Pay.
The number rolls down. Two months, gone in a second.
That means for millions of people, one dollar already costs about eight minutes of work.
Your curse wasn't a curse. It was a discount.
So tell me. If you could see the price of everything in minutes of your life, what would you stop buying first?
